title: DSL Rules
subject: gated-scoped-ac
summary: How to write what the engine reads: permissions, the three rule slots, the four operators, traversals and role forests, and what the loaders refuse.

axioms.text: A [[permission]] is a leaf: one entity, its actions, an optional field list, and the rules that narrow them.
A role is a branch of a [[role forest]]. It carries permissions and other roles, and holding it grants everything beneath it.
A condition is one subject, one operator and one operand. Nothing is inferred.
Config enters the engine through `registerPermissions` and `registerForests`, which refuse a malformed config when it loads.

purpose.intro: The shape `@libs/gated-scoped-ac` accepts for permissions, rules and roles, and what each part compiles to.
purpose.note: Why the DSL is shaped this way (AC23 to AC35) is in [[access-control|Access Control]]. The app's config is `shared/configs/access-control/index.ts`.

reference.statement: `definePermissions` takes a list of permissions and types each one by its actions.

imagesAndDiagrams.value:
| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `name` | unique across the whole config; `registerPermissions` throws on a duplicate |
| `entity` | a key of the `tables` map the app passes to `createAc` |
| `actions` | any of `create`, `read`, `update`, `delete` |
| `fields` | the columns read returns and update may write; absent or empty means every column |
| `rules` | OR-ed; a caller is granted what any rule that passes its context grants |

reference.statement: Rules and permissions widen what a caller gets; conditions within a slot narrow it.

claims.text: Rules in a permission are OR-ed, and so are the permissions a caller holds: every rule whose context passes adds its target to the scope.

A permission with `rules: []` grants nothing: the engine only collects rules that pass their context, and there are none. Every row is one rule with nothing in it: `rules: [{ context: [], target: [] }]`.
Field lists union across the permissions that contribute, and one contributing permission with no list means every column.

reference.statement: A rule is `{ context, target, payload? }`. Conditions within a slot are AND-ed, and each slot reads from one place.

claims.text: **context**: `bag:` conditions, checked in memory against the [[access context]] before anything else. A rule whose context fails is dropped. A context condition naming a `field:` never passes.
**target**: `field:` conditions, compiled to SQL against the entity's rows. An empty target means every row. `registerPermissions` refuses a target condition with no `field:`.

**payload**: `bag:` conditions on the row being created, read as `$requestBody.*`. Create-only: `registerPermissions` refuses a payload on a permission whose actions are anything but `["create"]`, and a payload condition with no `bag:`.
A create carries no target. `definePermissions` makes one a type error, and `registerPermissions` throws on it.

reference.statement: A condition names a subject, then exactly one of four operators with its operand.

claims.text: **Subject.** `field: "entity.column"` is a column of the rows being filtered. `bag: "$session.user.id"` is a value in the [[access context]]; the leading `$` is dropped and the dotted path walked.
**Operand.** `{ bag: "$…" }` for a path into the context, or `{ value: … }` for a string, number or boolean.
**Operators.** `is`, `isNot`, `has`, `hasNot`, and no others. In memory, `has` is membership when the subject is an array and equality otherwise; `is` is always equality.
`has` never means substring: a string is compared whole.
A `bag:` path that is unset or null fails the condition under every operator, negations included. See [[gated-scoped-ac-security|Security]].

imagesAndDiagrams.title: What each operator compiles to on a target
imagesAndDiagrams.value:
| Operator | On a single-value column | On an array or json column |
|---|---|---|
| `is` | `column = value` | refused when the engine is built |
| `isNot` | `column IS DISTINCT FROM value`, so a NULL column matches | refused when the engine is built |
| `has` | `column = value` | `value = ANY(column)`, or `column @> value::jsonb` |
| `hasNot` | `column IS NULL OR NOT (column = value)` | `column IS NULL OR NOT (…)` |
| any, with `value` unset or null | the rule is dropped | the rule is dropped |

reference.statement: A condition with `join` follows a value into another entity and filters there. What it compiles to depends on its subject.

claims.text: A `field:` subject (in a target) is a column of the filtered rows, so it compiles to `id IN (SELECT id FROM <entity> JOIN <join> ON <field> = <join>.<on> WHERE …)`.
A `bag:` subject (in a payload) is one value out of the context, so it compiles to a single existence check on `<join>`, run by the gate before the insert. An absent value denies.
`on` names the far-side column when it isn't `id`, as for a table keyed by its parent. Leave it out and the join lands on `id`.
`where` is one condition or a list of them, AND-ed, each naming a column of the joined entity. One hop only: a `where` condition cannot join again.

A traversal must be the only condition in its slot. Only the first one would be compiled, and anything beside it dropped, so `registerPermissions` refuses the config instead. Put further conditions in its `where`, or split them across rules.

reference.statement: Roles are declared as `RoleNode` trees: `{ role, permissions?, children? }`.

claims.text: `accountBaseline` is the forest of user roles any signed-in caller can hold. `forests[orgType]` is the forest of the organization type the caller acts in, read from the bag at `orgTypePath`.
A role grants its own `permissions` and those of every role beneath it. A branch may carry none of its own and exist only to imply its children.
A forest grants nothing by itself: a permission is collected only from a role the caller holds, and which roles that is, the app's hydration decides.
Role names are unique across every forest. `registerForests` throws on a duplicate and returns the flat list of roles.
`impliedRoles(assigned, forests)` returns the roles a set of roles implies, for a caller that gates on roles rather than on a verdict, such as navigation. It searches the forests it is given.

reference.statement: The config module runs the loaders at import, so a bad config fails the app's boot.

claims.text: `registerPermissions(lists, validator?)` merges the lists into a map by name. It throws on a duplicate name, a create with a target, a target condition with no `field:`, a slot holding a traversal beside other conditions, and a payload that is not on a create-only permission or has a condition with no `bag:`.
`registerForests({ accountBaseline, forests }, validator?)` throws on a role name used twice and returns `{ roles }`.
`validator` is optional: pass `zodConfigValidator()` from `@libs/gated-scoped-ac/zod` when the config does not come from type-checked TypeScript.
`createAc` adds one check of its own, because it is the first place that has the tables: `is` or `isNot` against an array or json column throws.
